title: Living Close to Rulers
note: He defines this as how ministers should conduct themselves with rulers. “The qualities rulers desire” were asked of the envoy, so this follows that chapter.

couplets.plain: Those who live close to quarrelsome rulers should be like people warming themselves at a fire, neither too far nor too near.
couplets.pm: Ministers who live close to quick-tempered rulers should stand midway, like people warming themselves at a fire. Go too far and the ruler gives you nothing. Go too near and he destroys you for disrespect. A fire too far leaves you cold, and a fire too near burns you.

links.quote: Those who live close to quarrelsome rulers
links.reason: Instructs whoever would live near rulers.
A fire warms at the right distance and burns when too near, and so does a ruler.

links.quote: neither too far nor too near

couplets.plain: Not wanting what rulers want will bring you lasting prosperity from those rulers.
couplets.pm: For ministers, not wanting what rulers want brings lasting wealth from those rulers. What they want here means what belongs to them alone: their pleasures, adornment and eminence. If ministers fear to rival them and don’t want these, the rulers are pleased and give all wealth themselves. To want these brings ruin.

links.reason: Reveals what brings lasting prosperity from rulers.

couplets.plain: If you guard yourself, guard against the grave faults. Once suspicion has set in, no one can easily clear it.
couplets.pm: Ministers who want to protect themselves should guard against grave faults, because once rulers hear of these and suspect, no one can reassure them. Grave faults are treachery, intimacy with the royal women and taking rare treasure. Even if you are cleared, it comes back whenever they see you, as a loan comes to mind on seeing the debtor.

couplets.plain: In the presence of the truly great, put a stop to whispers in the ear and shared laughter.
couplets.pm: When near rulers of full worth, don’t whisper in someone’s ear or laugh looking into someone’s face where they can see. If you do, they will take it that you did so because you saw some fault in them.

links.quote: In the presence of the truly great
put a stop to whispers in the ear and shared laughter
links.reason: Whispers and shared laughter near the great are slights to be avoided.

couplets.plain: Don’t listen in on anything, don’t press, and hear the secret when it is let out to you.
couplets.pm: When the ruler is in secret talk with others, don’t lend an ear to anything, even what might seem fit to hear, and don’t pursue him with questions. Hear that secret only when he himself tells it, holding nothing back.

couplets.plain: Read the signs, consider the time, and say what is needed and not disliked, in a way that pleases.
couplets.pm: When you speak to the ruler on business, read his present mood, watch for the right time, and say what he won’t dislike and what is needed, so that his mind wants it. Speaking while he is taken up with desire, anger and the like, or at an unfit time, is useless. What he rejects won’t go through. Use sweet, brief, clear words.

links.quote: Read the signs, consider the time
links.reason: Teaches one who must speak before a ruler how to choose his moment.

links.quote: Read the signs, consider the time
say what is needed and not disliked

couplets.plain: Say what is wanted. What is of no use, never say, even if asked.
couplets.pm: Say things of great use that the ruler wants, even if he hasn’t asked. Useless things, never say, even if he himself asks. “Never” includes times of want.

links.reason: Governs what may and may not be said before a ruler.

links.quote: What is of no use, never say, even if asked
links.reason: Even being asked is no reason to say what serves no purpose.

couplets.plain: Don’t scorn someone as young or as your kin. Live in keeping with the light that stands in them.
couplets.pm: Don’t scorn rulers, thinking “He is younger than us” or “He is our kin”. Act in keeping with the light in them. That light is their nature as gods, guarding the world even while they sleep. So act as though they are gods and you are mortals. The light has cast off their youth and kinship, and whoever scorns them for these will be cast off too.

links.quote: Don’t scorn someone as young or as your kin
links.reason: Warns those close to a ruler by age or kinship against familiarity.

links.quote: the light that stands in them
links.reason: Demands conduct fit for the light in a ruler, whatever his age or relation.

couplets.plain: Those of steady vision won’t think “We have been accepted” and do what isn’t acceptable.
couplets.pm: Those of steady understanding don’t think “The ruler esteems us” and then do what he doesn’t want. Those who ruin themselves in this way think of themselves, once favoured, as new men. Those who think of themselves as they were before, and go in fear, are the ones of steady vision.

links.reason: Shows how the clear-sighted carry themselves when a ruler has taken them up.
Favour is no licence: the wise still take care not to displease a ruler.

couplets.plain: The intimacy that says “We go back a long way” and does what isn’t fitting brings ruin.
couplets.pm: The licence that makes ministers think “We are old to the ruler” and do what doesn’t suit them brings them ruin. When he loses patience and strikes, he doesn’t look on that old bond with kindly regard, but takes their life. So don’t do what rulers hate, trusting that they will bear it.

links.quote: The intimacy that says “We go back a long way”
links.reason: Foretells the end of those who lean on closeness to a ruler.

links.quote: does what isn’t fitting brings ruin
links.reason: Long acquaintance gives no licence to slight a ruler: those who presume on it perish.
